chunks: 4 - Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (upon them be peace). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (upon him be peace) said:

I will surely describe Islam in a way that no one before me has described it, nor will anyone after me describe it: Islam is submission, and submission is sincerity, and sincerity is certainty, and certainty is performance, and performance is [good] action. Indeed, the believer takes his religion from his Lord and does not take it from his own opinion. O people, your religion, your religion! Hold fast to it, and let no one remove you from it, for a sin in it is better than a good deed in other than it, because a sin in it is forgiven, while a good deed in other than it is not accepted (3).

key_terms.التسليم: submission/surrender — the foundational act of yielding to divine authority

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali define Islam in a chain-like description, and what is the relationship between submission, sincerity, certainty, and action?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (as) gives a unique chain-definition of Islam, describing it as a progressive sequence: Islam is submission, submission is sincerity, sincerity is certainty, certainty is performance, and performance is action. He emphasizes that the believer derives his religion from his Lord, not from personal opinion. He then urges the people to hold fast to their religion, arguing that a sin committed within Islam is better than a good deed outside it, because sins in Islam can be forgiven while good deeds outside Islam are not accepted. This teaching was delivered through a chain of narrators tracing back through the Imams to Imam Ali himself.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi'l Qasim from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (as) said:

I will describe Islam in a way that no one before me nor after me has described it: Islam is submission, and submission is sincerity, and sincerity is certainty, and certainty is performance, and performance is [good] action. The believer takes his religion from his Lord and not his opinion. O people! Your religion, your religion! Hold onto it, and do not allow anyone to hinder you or remove you from it. A sin in Islam is better than a good deed in other religions, for a sin in Islam can be forgiven, while a good deed in another religion is not accepted.
